scope: All five essays read in full against Chinese source, 571 blocks including headings and edition notes. Episodes 1–3 reviewed first; episodes 4–5 subsequently read paragraph-by-paragraph against fact-corrected source. This is substantive prose review, not count-only verification.
findings_fixed: Episode 1: students invent bun names, not names for themselves.
Episode 2: poverty sentence refers to Shaoan household, not Xiulian herself.
Episode 2: ten-thousand-yuan household rendered as family annual income, not person equated to household.
Episodes 2–3: two editorial disclaimers naturalized while retaining narrative/interpretive limits.
Episode 4: nachjagen takes dative; corrected einem vermeintlich besseren Leben nachjagt.
Episode 5: witness sentence tells actual rescue without correcting an imaginary reader.
Episode 5: removed erroneous final railway-station departure; source independently corrected too.
source_checks: Bun nicknames; kiln years and illness without asserted medical causation; Fujun not party to marriage pressure; Xiaoxia recruitment and proposed transfer acknowledged; Wang saves An Suozi; Jin Xiu distinct from city-transfer proposal; actual final approach; Lu Yao four-year chronology.
interpretive_limits_retained: Runye debt/repayment explanation is the essay’s reading, not a general assertion about disability.
Xiaoxia death necessity remains a literary reading, not proof of historical impossibility.
The title and exclusivity language in episode 4 avoid idealizing her as wholly untouched by rank.
Episode 2 translates the supposed technician as incompetent rather than independently establishing criminal fraud; Chinese assertion not silently changed.
assessment: Narrative scenes and central argument preserved; no blocking omission or mistranslation found in final read. All claimed facts beyond this bounded source audit are not independently certified.
